text:
ryan: quick heads-up — nightly fused-attn run shows a ~12% token/sec regression at seq=4096, batch=8 on p4d. numbers from bench-run 2026-03-20 attached.

ajay: ugh. is this on the new routed-kernel switch or the tiling change from yesterday?

ryan: routed-kernel toggle off — still repros. suspecting shared memory tiling + KV cache interplay. noticed a spike in DRAM reads in the nvprof trace.

cheng: can you paste the perf lines?

ryan: ```
# baseline fused-attn (old tiling) - p4d, seq=4096, batch=8
tokens/s: 24.8k
DRAM throughput: 610 GB/s
shared mem util: 48%

# current (new tiling + routed kernels)
tokens/s: 21.8k
DRAM throughput: 680 GB/s
shared mem util: 33%
L2 reads up ~18%
```

maria: more DRAM, less sharedmem => kernel is spilling more to global memory. could be tiling causing register/shared-memory pressure and forcing extra loads.

ajay: also saw increased KV cache misses in the profiler for paged-attn path. That would surface as extra DRAM hotpath ops.

perf-bot: benchmark 1793245678 completed — summary: fused-attn-regression-4096 batch=8 — CI id 2026-03-20-07:23 (link: https://ci.redwood/bench/1793245678) :warning:

cheng: hypothesis: new tiling reduces per-warp shared mem reuse for QK compute and increases global reads when we materialize paged KV blocks. Two paths to validate: 1) run with old tiling parameters on the new kernel selection, 2) run with KV-cache disabled to see delta.

ryan: running both now. run ids: 1793245890 (old-tiling + new-routing), 1793246001 (kv-disabled + new-tiling).

ajay: when you run nv-nsight, capture these metrics: dram__throughput.average, l2_subp0_read_throughput, shared_load_transactions. that should show if we're seeing extra global loads instead of shared loads.

maria: if KV misses are the main culprit we might be able to bias batching heuristics: increase max-batch for seq=4096 so we amortize DRAM cost. but that hurts tail latency.

cheng: alternative: change pipeline staging so KV materialization happens earlier and overlaps with compute. add one more pipeline stage for page prefetching to hide DRAM latency. tradeoff is more register pressure.

ryan: quick diff from run 1793245890 (old-tiling): tokens/s = 24.1k (almost recovered), DRAM throughput = 615 GB/s, shared mem util = 46%. so old tiling looks much closer to baseline.

perf-bot: run 1793246001 (kv-disabled) finished: tokens/s = 25.0k, DRAM throughput = 590 GB/s.

ajay: interesting — disabling KV cache improved perf, which implies our paged-KV path has regression (not plain fused kernel math). maybe paged attention's block load routine changed with tiling.

maria: can you grep for the recent changes to paged-attn block loader? I recall a micro-optimization that moved a conditional inside the main loop (PR #4107).

ryan: checking... PR link: https://git.redwood/infra/attn-kernels/pull/4107 — it adjusted block copy for 128->64 tile pivot. reverting locally gives tokens/s ~24.7k.

cheng: plan: revert PR 4107 for now, add a regression test for paged-KV DRAM reads (metric threshold), and schedule a focused shared-memory tiling sweep to find tiling params that preserve shared reuse.

ajay: I'll own the tiling sweep. starting with tile widths {32,48,64,96,128} and pipeline stages {2,3,4}. run matrix on p4d and a100 (to check arch differences).

ryan: I'll opent a rollback PR for 4107 and add a benchmark job that runs seq={1024,2048,4096} batch={4,8,16} with dram+shared metrics exported. PR: https://git.redwood/infra/attn-kernels/pull/4112

maria: once PR lands let's gate the new routed-kernel by a perf flag so we can A/B with the old path in prod. also add a quick canary that checks token/sec and dram throughput on deploy.

ajay: one more data point: for seq=2048 we don't see regression (tokens/s +/-2%). suggests working set crosses a threshold around 3k-5k where sharedmem tiling matters.

cheng: good catch. that aligns with per-block KV tile size. also need to watch occupancy numbers — if we bump pipeline stages occupancy drops and may hurt small-batch throughput. include occupancy in sweep metrics.

ryan: action items:
- ajay: tiling + pipeline sweep (p4d/a100) — collect dram/l2/shared/occupancy per run (ETA ~6h)
- ajay: add metric thresholds to benchmark harness for paged-KV DRAM reads
- ryan: open rollback PR + canary job (done: #4112)
- cheng: rough design for prefetch pipeline stage and register pressure estimate (start PR if sweep fails)

maria: 👍 thanks. please drop links to run artifacts here so we can triage next week.

perf-bot: sweep jobs enqueued: 1793247000..1793247600 (5 runs).

ajay: starting first run now. will post CSVs and perf flamegraphs as they finish. :coffee:

ryan: thanks — this was the missing link. sounds like tiling change + paged-KV micro-opt combined to push more load to DRAM. we'll revert and rework with the sweep data.

maria: +1. keep ownership chain clear and let's avoid rerolling tuned kernels without a perf gate.

ajay: noted, will include gating thresholds in PR.
